angleRead.text: The 2041 line is the hinge. 136.1 innings is a 22-start season, not a 33-start season, and the walk rate that makes the K/BB ratio look elite — 1.6 per nine — is the smallest sample on the dossier. The strikeout rate is stable across eight seasons; the walk rate is not. 2039 and 2038 both carried sub-2.0 walk rates across 180-plus innings, so 2041 is not unprecedented. But 2040's 2.9 per nine is the outlier on the low side of control, and it came in a full season. The claim the numbers carry: Rivas is a command pitcher whose walk rate is the variable, and 2041's 5.54 K/BB is a rate built on a partial season, not a new identity. checks: State the sample size: 136.1 innings, 22 starts, versus 180-plus in each of the prior three full seasons.
Show the walk-rate spread: 1.6 in 2041, 2.9 in 2040, 1.8 in 2039, 1.9 in 2038.
Place the peer band: Ramos at 1.7 BB/9 over 212.2 IP, Dillon at 3.9 over 150.1 IP.
Name the disconfirming number: a 2042 walk rate at or under 1.8 per nine across 180-plus innings.

plan.interpretation: The 2041 ERA and K/BB ratio will be read as a breakout. The data says the strikeout rate is flat and the walk rate is the only thing that moved, and it moved in a season 47 innings shorter than the three before it. That is variance, not identity, until a full season repeats it.
unverifiedLead: Whether Rivas's 2041 season was shortened by injury or by workload management is not on the dossier; the innings count is the only fact.
